entities.name: Turbo Puffer
entities.how_described: 本集说它是一个搜索引擎，写入直接进对象存储、无共识协议，围绕最小化往返次数和内存层级设计，让多租户隔离与加密天然成立。

evidence.quote: I'm the CEO and co-founder of Turbo Puffer, a search engine that we work with Legora and others on.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Yeah, so I was talking about why the company is called Turbo Puffer, another talk here earlier today, but one of the other explanations of the name of Turbo Puffer is that it's about puffing into the different memory hierarchies and really mastering when data should be in particular memory hierarchies.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Turbo Puffer is a database that is really designed around the memory hierarchy and all of the smarts in Turbo Puffer is that all of these namespaces are puffed in and out of the cache.

entities.name: 对象存储 (object storage)
entities.how_described: 本集说 Turbo Puffer 写入直接进 S3、基于 blob 查询，冷数据静静躺在对象存储里，是整个架构经济性与合规隔离的根基。

evidence.quote: We check the memory cache for any objects, NVMe SSD cache, and then finally to object storage.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: The problem with a graph on something like object storage or disk, again, we want to have things as far down that memory hierarchy as possible.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

entities.name: 智能体 (agent)
entities.how_described: 本集说智能体时代单次 RAG 查询不够——一个智能体要做 20 次、100 次查询，检索延迟会累加，所以为智能体优化检索尤其要命。

evidence.quote: So obviously this is a huge thing when you're doing, I mean, one thing is if you're doing a single sort of RAG style thing, but if you have an agent that does 20 queries, 100 queries, these really, really add up.

entities.name: 命名空间 (namespace)
entities.how_described: 本集说 namespace 是 Turbo Puffer 的「表」概念、分离的原子单元——每个项目/司法辖区一个命名空间，可独立加密、放独立 bucket。

evidence.quote: And what we did with TurboPuffer was we did one namespace per project.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: The query reaches some namespace and namespace is kind of our concept of a table.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Well, Oblix Storage Native, if you design it around the atomic unit of separation being the namespace or the table, every single table could be encrypted with a different key.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: Every single namespace could be in a different bucket.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_00

evidence.quote: You can do whatever configuration that you need at the namespace level.

entities.name: 内存层级 (memory hierarchy)
entities.how_described: 本集说 Turbo Puffer 的核心是「向不同内存层级里吹气」：热数据常驻 DRAM、叶子节点留 SSD、冷数据沉到对象存储，追求最佳性能成本比。

evidence.quote: Turbo Puffer is a database that is really designed around the memory hierarchy and all of the smarts in Turbo Puffer is that all of these namespaces are puffed in and out of the cache.

evidence.quote: The problem with a graph on something like object storage or disk, again, we want to have things as far down that memory hierarchy as possible.

evidence.quote: And so you're trying to shrink the diameter of the graph, you're trying to do all these tricks to make the graph, but fundamentally you're at odds with the fact that a graph is about a random sequential trade-off that you have in memory and in registers, but not further down the memory hierarchy.

evidence.quote: And so we started on Elasticsearch for this, but also moving to TurboPuffer.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: Elasticsearch just got extremely expensive because we have to have everything there.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: If we had to have separate Elasticsearch databases for each of these, it would be just hell.

entities.name: Postgres
entities.how_described: 本集说 Legora 曾用 Postgres + PG Vector 做搜索、4000 个分区装箱项目，但冷热项目混在同一分区导致缓存抖动、P99 从 100 毫秒飙到 20 秒。

evidence.quote: So we moved from Elasticsearch to Postgres.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And I imagine a bunch of you guys are like, why would you ever put your vectors into Postgres?
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And the reason that we did this was we were already using Postgres for OLTP workloads.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so it was really easy for us to try to shift all of our search into Postgres as well because then we only have one system.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: And so when we queried them, Postgres would pull the partition, put it into memory, we'd do the stuff, and then we queried another partition and another partition, and it would essentially thrash the cache all the time.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01

evidence.quote: You know, we didn't have to have a bunch of different ones, like with Postgres, and it would, since it's blob-based, it could just query the blobs that we had anyway.
evidence.speaker: SPEAKER_01
